metadata.note: The Litchfield and Madison corridor (CB&Q Junction, Litchfield - Madison - Bridge Junction, East St. Louis) as two single-year anchors on shared geometry: Litchfield and Madison 1907 [ANCHOR] (court-ordered passenger service c.1906-1908) and its predecessor the Chicago, Peoria & St. Louis 1891 [ANCHOR] (through Chicago/Springfield - St. Louis trains after the Nov 1890 opening). Rule 4: one feature per operator.
metadata.ownership_split: CP&StL built and ran the line 1890 - c.1898 (Jacksonville South-Eastern group to 1893, receivers thereafter); Litchfield and Madison Railway from 1900, with the CP&StL operating it under lease Mar 1900 - Jun 1904 (no passenger trains confirmed in that window, so no drawable split); merged into the C&NW 2 Jan 1958 with no passenger service.
metadata.omitted: Block [3], Illinois Central (and possibly Nickel Plate) trackage-rights trains Glen Carbon - Madison from the 1920s: another road's trains, already drawn in illinois_central_st_louis_division.geojson; not an L&M feature. The 1926 C&NW Benld connection (freight only). The 1909-1914 time-card trains (reported annulled daily). The March 1915 revival special (one night). The 1912 'gasoline motor car' (not shown to be public service). Bridge Junction - St. Louis Union Station (TRRA).
metadata.freight_only_check: Both features are single proven passenger years. Everything after c.1908 was freight-only (Feb 1952 Official Guide daggers every L&M station 'For freight only'); abandonment years (Litchfield - Mount Olive 1961, Mount Olive - DeCamp 1970) are not passenger years and are not drawn.

properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced, no straight-line legs: 48.9 mi CB&Q Junction (Litchfield) - Bridge Junction (East St. Louis), of which 44.3 mi CB&Q Jct - Madison. Documented: 47.3 mi CB&Q Jct - Madison and 51.0 mi to Bridge Junction (Fowler, branchline.uk table 212); about 44 mi of route owned (Wikipedia); Litchfield - Bridge Junction about 48 mi for the CP&StL (Fowler table 197A). The trace is 6% short of Fowler's CB&Q Jct - Madison figure and matches the owned-route figure; the difference is not resolved. Trace: opstrace.py over OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator='Litchfield and Madison' (38.6 mi; razed grade Litchfield - Mount Olive - Staunton, MCT Quercus Grove and Nickel Plate trail grade Worden - Edwardsville - Glen Carbon, the 'C&NW SI Line' and UP Madison Subdivision / 'UP (CNW) Main' Glen Carbon - Madison), with untagged OSM rail and OpenHistoricalMap ways bridging gaps in that tagging (10.5 mi). About 42 of the 44.3 Litchfield - Madison miles lie within 120 m of L&M-tagged ways; the off-tag stretches are 0.3 mi at Edwardsville and 1.8 mi between Glen Carbon and the 'C&NW SI Line' (a sparse OHM way, within about 150 m of the tagged grade). The trace deliberately avoids the parallel Illinois Central grade (MCT Heritage Trail), the Wabash (NS Brooklyn District) and the 1926 C&NW Benld connection ('Monterey Branch', freight-only, also L&M-tagged south of Staunton). Madison - Bridge Junction (4.5 mi as drawn, about 3.7 documented) is TRRA track (Illinois Transfer and Eads Subdivisions as OSM has them today), a shortest path through the East St. Louis terminal; the Bridge Junction pin (east end of the Eads Bridge approach, 38.6264,-90.1654) is approximate and not sourced to a map. The line stops on the Illinois bank and does not cross the river (the Eads Bridge leg to St. Louis Union Station was TRRA). North end pinned at the L&M - CB&Q (BNSF Beardstown Subdivision) crossing south of Litchfield; the Litchfield depot itself, reached over the Burlington, is not drawn. LATER ALIGNMENT: this is the line as OSM records it at abandonment / today, not checked against an 1891 or 1907 map; the East St. Louis approach in particular is the present-day TRRA layout. The Litchfield - Staunton razed way is a sparse OSM drawing (73 nodes over about 20 mi).
properties.documented_mileage: 47.3 mi CB&Q Jct - Madison, 51.0 mi to Bridge Junction (Fowler table 212); about 44 mi owned (Wikipedia)

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Court-ordered passenger service. The L&M had become a coal road running no passenger trains; Edwardsville-area citizens sued for mandamus (May 1905) and the Illinois Supreme Court upheld the order on 14 June 1906. 'Following the order the officials ran a passenger train, but it failed to pay' (Daily Journal, East St. Louis, 17 Sep 1914); by March 1915 the road 'has not run a passenger train for the public in seven years' (same paper, 8 Mar 1915), i.e. last public train about 1908. 1907 is the only year inside that window under every reading, so this is a one-year ANCHOR: service certainly ran somewhat wider (some part of 1906-1908), but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen it. Do NOT draw 1909-1914 off the printed time card: the Jan 1910 Official Guide (p.878) shows a daily Madison - C.B.&Q. Junction round trip, but in June 1914 the paper reported the listed trains were 'annulled by the chief dispatcher as a regular order of business each morning' (SOURCE CONFLICT recorded, newspapers followed). The single March 1915 revival-meeting special is not a service span and is not drawn. Freight (coal and C&NW/IC bridge traffic) continued to the 1958 C&NW merger; Litchfield - Mount Olive abandoned 1961. Mileage: L&M trains reached the Litchfield depot over the Burlington from CB&Q Junction. Headway is a guess from 'a passenger train' (one daily round trip), not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: Chronicling America newspapers for the 1906 court order, the 'seven years' end and the 1914 annulled trains; the 1907 year is an inference from them, not a dated timetable. Headway NOT SOURCED.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] The Chicago, Peoria & St. Louis built Litchfield - Madison 1889-1890 and opened the connection to East St. Louis in November 1890; in December 1890 it began, with the Santa Fe, a through Pullman service Chicago - St. Louis (Wikipedia, CP&StL, citing Commercial and Architectural St. Louis (1891) pp.31-32), and this was its only St. Louis entry - though Wikipedia does not say in so many words that the service ran via Litchfield - Madison. 1891, the first full year, is the one year taken as proven. Service certainly ran wider (Fowler 197A: 'former route until c.1898'), but no other year is confirmed and the c.1898 end is Fowler's approximation. Do not widen without an 1890s timetable. Trains continued Bridge Junction - St. Louis Union Station over the Terminal Railroad Association (Eads Bridge); that leg is TRRA's and is not drawn. The CP&StL also operated the line under lease from the Litchfield and Madison Mar 1900 - Jun 1904, with no passenger trains found in those years. Headway is a guess (assumes a couple of daily through trains), not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia (CP&StL) for the Nov/Dec 1890 opening and through service; Fowler table 197A for the route. NOT SOURCED at timetable level - no 1890s Official Guide checked. Headway NOT SOURCED.
